- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment >0.8) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward; if below, adjust upward — especially if sentiment is weak.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen momentum in later days if sentiment cools.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.5), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true reversal point.
